intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis-4 (FHL4) is caused by homozygous mutation in the gene encoding syntaxin-11 (STX11) on chromosome 6q24.

paragraphs.text: Familial hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (FHL) is a rare autosomal recessive disorder characterized by hyperactive phagocytes and defects in natural killer (NK) cell function (zur Stadt et al., 2005). It presents in young children as a severe hyperinflammatory syndrome with activated macrophages and T lymphocytes (Zur Stadt et al., 2006). FHL4, caused by mutation in STX11, accounts for only a small fraction of FHL patients, and compared with other FHL subtypes, patients with STX11 nonsense mutations typically have less severe disease (Müller et al., 2014).

paragraphs.text: Rudd et al. (2006) studied the clinical features of 6 children with STX11 mutations from 4 families. Three patients had long periods (1 year or more) in remission without specific treatment, which the authors noted is very uncommon in this disease. Despite this milder phenotype, some children with STX11 mutations developed severe psychomotor retardation, and 2 of the 6 patients developed myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) or acute myelogenous leukemia (AML). The authors suggested that STX11 mutations may be associated with secondary hematopoietic malignancies.

paragraphs.text: Müller et al. (2014) described 3 children from unrelated consanguineous Pakistani families who presented with HLH. Two males were diagnosed at ages 2 months and 5 years, and a female at 48 months. The 2 patients with available clinical data had fever, splenomegaly, hepatomegaly, anemia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, hypertriglyceridemia, hypofibrinogenemia, and hyperferritinemia; hemophagocytosis was not observed, and neither had neurologic manifestations. Both were treated with dexamethasone, cyclosporine A, and etoposide and were in remission at 2 months, but both died; 1 had undergone hematopoietic stem cell transplantation at 15 months. The third patient was lost to follow-up. All 3 patients had deficient NK cell cytotoxicity against K562 target cells and deficient NK cell degranulation, which were partially restored by IL-2 stimulation; expression of perforin, granzyme B, and CD107a in NK cells was normal.

paragraphs.text: In 3 children from unrelated consanguineous Pakistani families with HLH, Müller et al. (2014) sequenced UNC13D, STX11, and STXBP2 and identified a homozygous c.173T-C mutation in the STX11 gene, resulting in a leu58-to-pro (L58P) substitution in the N-terminal Habc domain. The parents were heterozygous. Syntaxin-11 expression was greatly reduced in PBMCs and LAK cells from 1 patient, whereas Munc18-2 levels were similar to controls. In transfected HEK-293T cells, the L58P mutant was expressed at levels comparable to wildtype but did not bind Munc18-2; an engineered N-terminal R4A mutant also failed to bind Munc18-2, whereas the C-terminal Q268X mutation previously associated with FHL4 did not impair Munc18-2 binding. One patient was also heterozygous for a rare UNC13D variant (P271S) and homozygous for an uncommon UNC13D variant (R928C); this patient presented at an earlier age and showed less restoration of NK cell degranulation upon IL-2 stimulation, and the authors suggested that the UNC13D variants might contribute to disease severity.

(2005) noted that both STX11 and UNC13D are involved in vesicle trafficking and membrane fusion, and concluded that, besides perforin mutations, defects in the endocytotic or exocytotic pathway may be a common mechanism in FHL. (2020) reported an open-label, single-group, phase 2-3 study of emapalumab, a human anti-interferon-gamma antibody, given with dexamethasone to 34 patients 18 years of age or younger with primary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (27 previously treated and 7 previously untreated). A response occurred in 63% of previously treated patients and in 65% of all patients who received emapalumab, and 65% of patients who received emapalumab were able to proceed to transplantation. Severe infections developed in 10 patients during treatment. The abstract did not report results by genetic subtype.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of a large consanguineous Kurdish kindred with FHL4, zur Stadt et al. (2005) identified a homozygous 5-bp deletion in the STX11 gene. Syntaxin-11 protein was absent in the mononuclear cell fraction of homozygous patients. The deletion was also found in the homozygous state in 2 additional consanguineous Turkish/Kurdish FHL kindreds.

paragraphs.text: In 3 children from unrelated consanguineous Pakistani families with FHL4, Müller et al. (2014) identified a homozygous c.173T-C transition in the STX11 gene, resulting in a leu58-to-pro (L58P) substitution in the N-terminal Habc domain. The parents were heterozygous. Syntaxin-11 expression was greatly reduced in patient lymphocytes, and NK cell degranulation was defective. In transfected HEK-293T cells, the mutant protein was expressed at wildtype levels but did not bind Munc18-2.

agent.process_note: Read all 5 files in full: 4 abstracts and the full text of Müller et al. (2014). The abstracts give no nucleotide-level details for the 5-bp deletion or the C-terminal nonsense mutation that zur Stadt et al. (2005) reported, so those variants are named without HGVS. The nonsense mutation got no allelic-variant entry because the abstract does not name it. Müller et al. (2014) mention a Q268X mutation previously associated with FHL4, but I did not link it to zur Stadt's nonsense mutation. Rudd et al. (2006) do not name their 2 mutations in the abstract. The emapalumab paper covers primary HLH in general and gives no results by genotype. No HGNC reference data was supplied, so no gene MIM number is given.
